objectives: I can name 6 family members in English.
I can say He is... or She is... about a family member.
I can understand a short family description and find key information.
I can introduce a family member in two sentences.

stages.name: Opening — Retrieval and Bridge
stages.purpose: Activate am/is/are from the 09:00 slot through quick retrieval, then bridge to the new goal: using is to describe family members.

procedure.text: Hold up fingers: 1 finger = I, 2 fingers = you, 3 fingers = he or she. Pupils call back the correct verb: am, are, is. Demonstrate once, then run at speed.
Quick-fire drill: teacher holds up finger signals in random order, 10 rounds. Pupils call back am / are / is as a class.
Think-write: Write 2 sentences from memory. Sentence 1 about yourself (I am...). Sentence 2 about a classmate (Name is...). No board, no book.
Partner swap: check each other's sentences. Is am / is / are correct? Circle any errors.

Bridge: Say — You can talk about yourself and a friend. Now we go further. Today you will introduce your family. You will use is for your mum, your dad, your sister, your brother. Write on board: I can name 6 family members. I can say He is... or She is...

stages.name: Vocabulary — My Family
stages.purpose: Activate the 6 core family member words through listening, repetition, and a quick picture drill before pupils meet them in the reading text.

procedure.text: Write on board in two columns: English | Deutsch. Add one word at a time: mum / Mama, dad / Papa, brother / Bruder, sister / Schwester, grandma / Oma, grandpa / Opa. Say each English word aloud. Pupils repeat three times.
Point out cognates: grandma sounds like Oma, grandpa sounds like Opa — easy to remember! Bruder and Schwester are different, so practise those more.
Cover-and-recall: pupils cover the German column. Teacher points to an English word, pupils say the German. Then swap: cover English, pupils say the English from the German.
Quick model sentence: point to each word and say This is my sister. She is 8 years old. Pupils repeat.

stages.name: Grammar — He is / She is
stages.purpose: Recap the is rule and extend it explicitly to he/she family descriptions, with the German L1 contrast note preempting the sie confusion.

procedure.text: Open the grammar card: He is / She is — talking about your family. Read aloud together. Stress: She is for a girl or woman. He is for a boy or man. Point to the board: Er ist = He is. Sie ist = She is. Same idea as German!
Write on board: My sister is 8. She is 8. My dad is 40. He is 40. Elicit each sentence by pointing to a pupil: What do we say for my sister? Pupils complete.
Mini whiteboard / paper: teacher says a family member word (brother, mum, grandpa), pupils write He is or She is on their mini board and hold up.
Scan boards. Correct any He/She confusion aloud: grandpa is a man, so He is. Grandma is a woman, so She is.

stages.name: Reading — My Family
stages.purpose: Provide a controlled-vocabulary model text showing he is / she is in a family description context, building listening comprehension before guided practice.

procedure.text: Say: I will read a short text about a girl named Lena and her family. Listen and count: how many family members does Lena have? Read the text aloud clearly at slow pace.
Pupils read the text silently. Then answer two questions on paper: (1) How old is Lena's sister Anna? (2) Where is Lena's dad from?
Check whole-class. Write answers on board: Anna is 7. Lena's dad is from Leipzig. Ask: which verb did we use? Pupils identify is in each answer.
Point out the pattern: This is my ___ . He/She is ___ years old. Circle these sentences in the text on the board.

stages.name: Gap-fill — My Family
stages.purpose: Guided written practice of family vocabulary and am/is at sentence level, with German hints to scaffold without removing cognitive effort.

procedure.text: Say: Complete 5 sentences. Each blank has a German hint in brackets — use it to help you choose the right word. Work alone.
Pupils complete the 5-item gap-fill independently. Each blank has one answer. German hint provided for every blank.
Check whole-class. For each answer ask: Who wrote sister? Who wrote dad? Write correct answers on board. For the am/is items, ask: why am and not is? Pupils explain: I use am for I.

stages.name: Wrap-up
stages.purpose: Self-assessment against the lesson learning intentions and preview of the next lesson's listening task.

procedure.text: Point to I can... list on board. Thumbs up = yes, thumbs sideways = almost, thumbs down = not yet. Count responses for each statement.
Say: Next lesson you will hear someone describe their family. You will listen and write down the names and ages. Think about the words you learned today — you will need them!

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: keep the 6 family words visible on their desk (word card strip) during gap-fill and reading; during mini-whiteboard drill allow 3 seconds extra before holding up. Stronger pupils: after the gap-fill, write 2 extra sentences about a real family member without looking at the board; during wrap-up, attempt to introduce one family member aloud to a partner in 2 sentences.
exercisePlan: Gap-fill (Guided): 5 sentences — complete family member word or am/is verb form, German hint per blank [fk.w.introduce_self, fk.g.simple_present]
